doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Shearing's success and Tony Scott's welcome to New York
summary: Shearing's group topped the polls but was demanding to tour with; Tony Scott introduced Toots around.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. [laughs] Okay. So, so this was a major gig ‘cause George is touring all over.
That was the number one jazz group in the polls, and he had… There was a great job and not so easy for a family life, either. You travel all the time.

And then I met [inaudible] Tony Scott, I told you, you know. He was very… he was a typical Chamber of Commerce or welcome committee—one man welcome committee. For, like, in those days Al Foster, who played first saxophone and arranger for Count Basie. He also came to New York, and we had [inaudible/overlapping voices].
Maybe Frank Foster, not Al Foster? Uh, Frank Foster.
He’s the drummer, right. So Frank Foster, right.
Frank. Yeah. And I remember, yeah. He had a loft somewhere in the Village. Tony Scott and… that’s it. [laughs]
